recipes.name: Greek Penne and Chicken
ingredients_raw: 1 pound skinless, boneless chicken breast halves - cut into bite-size pieces
1 (14 ounce) can artichoke hearts in water

steps.text: In a large pot with boiling salted water cook penne pasta until al dente. Drain.

Meanwhile, in a large skillet over medium-high heat melt butter, add onion and garlic and cook for 2 minutes. Add chopped chicken and continue cooking, stirring occasionally until golden brown, about 5 to 6 minutes.

Reduce heat to medium- low. Drain and chop artichoke hearts and add them, chopped tomato, feta cheese, fresh parsley, lemon juice, dried oregano, and drained penne pasta to the large skillet. Cook until heated through, about 2 to 3 minutes.
Season with salt and ground black pepper. Serve warm.

raw_recipe.headline: Greek Penne and Chicken
raw_recipe.description: This is one of my favorite ‘stand by’ recipes. I keep the ingredients on hand to make a quick, delicious, satisfying meal.

video.description: See how to make a Greek-influenced chicken pasta that’s bursting with flavor. Artichokes, feta cheese, tomatoes, and red onion combine in a light sauce with lemon juice and dried oregano.

review.reviewBody: FIrst time I made this it was very bland and didn't have too much sauce to cover the pasta. Second time it was amazing, I made a few revisions. I used marinated artichoke hearts (this is VERY important if you want good flavor) and cooked the garlic and onion in a mix of olive oil and some of the marinade from the artichokes. No butter, didn't need it. I added a six ounce can of tomato paste so there was a good amount of sauce and I used a full cup of feta. I added half the feta when the recipe calls for it, then right before serving I sprinkled the other half on top, covered the pan and let the cheese melt a bit. Second time around the recipe was delicious!

this was great..... with a few tweaks......added a half a red pepper, diced, to the onions and garlic...... added two or three good handfuls of spinach after the onions/garlic/peppers were sauteed..... used a can of diced tomatoes and about 7 cherry tomatoes that were hanging out in my frig instead of a diced roma tomato, added halved kalamata olives and..... most importantly, I zested the lemon and added the zest to the dish with the lemon juice for really good lemon pasta.

I liked this recipe but thought it was a little bland. I followed a mixture of the original recipe and some of the suggestions by other reviewers as well as adding a few things of my own. I do not like artichokes so I did not use them. I only used 8 oz. of pasta which was plenty. I used the juice of half a lemon which I think may have been a tad to much. Doubled the garlic and cubed 2 big chicken breasts. Used I cup of chicken broth, 1 13 oz can of diced tomatoes in sauce and a couple of splashes of heavy cream which really made the sauce creamy. I also cut up and slightly steamed a bunch of asparagus and added to the dish towards the end. I added a little bit pepper flakes in addition to some extra oregano and basil. It was good but feel it needed a boost of flavor

This is a great base recipe that can be modified according to what you have on hand. I didn't have all the ingredients so I modified it. First I used lingunie pasta instead of penne. I cooked my chicken breast in the oil from the marinated artichoke hearts and seasoned it with garlic-paprika seasoning. When the chicken was cooked I removed it from the pan and added garlic to saute for about 4 minutes. Then I put the chopped chicken and artichoke hearts in the pan. I added a half cup of white wine and let it reduce. Once reduced (about 8 minutes on med-high) I added a half can of whole black olives and 2 T of capers. I also added 1 T of balsamic vinegar, a dash of chicken bouillon, and 1 T of lemon juice from plastic lemon for flavor. So basically I didn't use butter, onion, tomatoes, feta cheese, or parsley and it still turned out great! I know I made a lot of modifications, but that's what makes this an awesome recipe.. It's veratile! So, bon apetit!

Wonderful flavor!!!! I did take others suggestions and used a can of diced tomatoes istead of a whole tomato. I also used olive oil & some of the marinade from the artichokes to cook the onions, garlic and then added more of the marinade when I added the chicken. It gave it great flavor. I also seasoned the chicken before adding to skillet. If you find it still a little dry, add some of the water used to cooked the penne into the mixture. I didn't need to do this but the water used to cook pasta adds nice flavor and moisture to most pasta sauces. I also doubled the feta and saved half to top the pasta and used only 12 oz of pasta (MAKES PLENTY). My whole family LOVED this dish! It makes WAY more than 4 servings.

Loved this! I did make a few changes, some because of other comments and others because of what I had on hand. I did use marinated artichokes and marinated the chicken pieces in the oil for about 60 minutes. I used a can of diced tomatoes (what I had on hand) and as I didn't have any lemon, I added about a cup of Greek olives, halved. I think they added the zip that I would have missed without the lemon. I also added extra feta cheese when serving. My 14 year old had three helpings!

I found this recipe about 6 years ago and made it originally for my boyfriend (now husband) who is of Greek heritage. We absolutely love it! Everyone I've made it for loves it. Fantastic recipe, thank you! My only tweak is to use marinated artichokes and dump in the entire 12 oz. including marinade. I'm just making it now for his birthday dinner.

I found a Greek marinade for the chicken - made it in the morning to marinate in the fridge during the day. I also got the marinated artichokes as commenters recommended. Served it to my husband and two guests - instant favorite.

You know, I liked this. I followed the recommendations to sautée the garlic and onion in the liquid from the marinated artichoke hearts. Quite good.

In addition I increased the amount of feta and added as suggested. Tomato paste was also used with the two Roma tomatoes. 

It was quite good. I would cut the pasta in half though. I do not see how this is 4 servings. More like 8 actually.

I've been making this for my family the past few years, we like it because it has such a different taste than our other meals, the lemon and feta are really great!
Changes made: used 12 oz pkg of penne pasta (still has more pasta than other ingredients), cut chicken into small bite-sized pieces (so they mix in with other ingredients better), instead of a tomato I used a can of diced tomatoes, I added 1/2 the feta while mixing, and 1/2 on top before serving, I also added 1/4 cup green olives.

Outstanding flavor mix in this dish. But yes, as others have said, use about half as much pasta. (I always allow 2 oz. per serving.) And when you get it all mixed together in the last step, if you think it's a little lacking in "sauce," just add some hot pasta water or hot chicken broth. Oh, and I used cherry tomatoes in place of the chopped tomato, since most grocery store tomatoes are so hard and tasteless.
Delicious and easy to make. The only thing I changed was I used a half can of fire roasted diced tomatoes instead of fresh tomatoes.

This is delicious! I made it exactly as written the first time and it was fantastic. But I love feta, so I dump an entire tub of crumbled feta in. I also use a whole, small red onion rather than just a half cup.
My family absolutely loves this dish, followed the recipe completely
Very good combination of flavors
It was easy and very good. I made it a little easier by using left over grilled chicken.
This was super easy and even more tasty. 10/10 would recommend!!
This was a delightful and light dish and perfect for the summer!
Yum. I used one jar with liquid of Marinated artichokes and one 14.5 ounce can of drained diced tomatoes instead of fresh. Added more feta.
Used 1/4 fewer penne noodles. Added one can of diced tomatoes with Italian seasoning along with a 1/4 cup of chicken broth, along with marinated artichoke hearts. Delicious
